title: AI helped build my Roblox game, but real playtests exposed the confusing parts
author: Tibor_tester
selftext:
I’m making a Roblox game where you buy meme viruses from a train, bring them home to earn coins, and steal or defend collections. You can also infect someone’s in-game computer with effects. It’s free to play, with optional purchases.



I use AI extensively for the coding. The biggest lesson so far has been that a feature working in a Studio test doesn’t mean it works well for a new player. Playing on PC while my brother played on a phone exposed awkward aiming, crowded UI and tutorial steps that weren’t clear. Feedback also pushed me away from adding features and toward making the opening easier to follow. Multiplayer bugs are still being worked on.



If you try it, I’d really appreciate knowing whether you understand what to do and whether the collecting/stealing loop is fun. Where would you stop playing? I’d also be interested in how other AI-using developers test this gap between ‘it works’ and ‘it makes sense’.



[https://www.roblox.com/games/83980471718380/Hack-Their-PC](https://www.roblox.com/games/83980471718380/Hack-Their-PC)



Thanks for taking a look. This is an unpaid feedback request.

comments.author: LocoPwnify
comments.body:
If your tutorial sucks no one will see your endgame. 

The beginning of game needs to grip you.

comments.author: PurchaseCommercial34
comments.body: for the 'it works' vs 'it makes sense' gap, the cheapest thing on roblox is probably funnel events. AnalyticsService has LogOnboardingFunnelStepEvent, you fire it at each tutorial step and the creator dashboard shows how many people reach each one, so you can see which step actually loses them instead of guessing from one playtest. the other cheap one, for stuff like the phone aiming, is watching someone play without saying anything and noting every spot where they stop moving for more than a few seconds. those pauses tend to be the confusing bits, even if they don't bring them up afterwardsfor the 'it works' vs 'it makes sense' gap, the cheapest thing on roblox is probably funnel events.
